title: Reveal in order, keep everything shown
statement: Reveal a screen's parts in order, never take away anything that has appeared, and offer the way on only once everything on the page has been seen.
detail: The Grade 9 prototype reveals each screen's parts in order, each when the student asks for it, with nothing on a timer; nothing that has appeared goes away, Next appears only once everything on the page has been seen, and because the reveal count lives in the session, a refresh resumes on the same part and coming back shows everything already seen. A younger-grade checklist of lesson invariants has every step, chart row, hint rung and sub-thought arrive on exactly one Next tap, checked by a scripted walk, and the younger-grade audio rules hide the Next button while the voice is sounding. No source measures the effect on learners.
against: No source measures the effect on learners.

evidence.quote: Every screen reveals its parts in order, and the student asks for each one ("Then what happened?", "Show her proof").
Nothing is on a timer, nothing that has appeared goes away, and Next only appears once everything on the page has been seen.
so a refresh resumes on the same part and coming Back shows everything already seen.
**E1. Reveal on Next, everywhere, both modes.** Every step, chart row, ladder rung and sub-thought arrives on exactly one Next tap; the voice never reveals or advances.
The same button must not exist while the voice is sounding, and neither must an armed microphone.
